title: Existence of compatible alternating injective resolution rows
statement: Let $B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $K$ be a $\mathbb Z$-indexed cochain complex with $K^p=0$ for $p<0$, and let $S$ be its image under the single-degree-zero functor $B\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(B,\mathbb N)$. There is a compatible row system $R$ for $S$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-rows] such that $A^p=0$ for $p<0$, each of $A^p,Z^p,D^p,H^p$ has injective terms, and each of its four augmentations $j_A^p,j_Z^p,j_D^p,j_H^p$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. This asserts only existence of the row system, not any identification with the cycles, images or homology of its associated complex.

proof.text: Obtain compatible boundary/cycle/homology resolutions from the object-resolution-row theorem. In particular the boundary resolution is zero for p<=0 and the cycle resolution is zero for p<0.

Form the short exact row Z^p(K) -> K^p -> B^(p+1)(K) using the boundary projection. Compare it to iCycles followed by d via the mono image inclusion to transfer exactness of the kernel sequence. The projection is epi by image factorization. Apply prescribed horseshoe in each p with the already chosen cycle and next-boundary resolutions. Its degreewise short exactness gives exact rows of complexes. For p<0 the endpoint complexes are zero, and the middle term resolution is therefore zero.

For the exact functor F=single0, use ShortComplex.mapCyclesIso, PreservesImage.iso, and the mapped left homology data followed by F.mapIso(leftHomologyIso) to identify the prolonged source cycles, images and homology with F of the original objects. The homology projection square follows from LeftHomologyData.homologyπ_comp_homologyIso_hom and preservation of composition. Precompose the chosen resolution augmentations with these isomorphisms.

Assemble CartanEilenbergRows with both exact rows and these four augmentations. The cycle and homology squares follow from the horseshoe squares and the transport identities. Compose the boundary-to-cycle augmentation square with the cycle-to-term square to get commD. The term-to-next-boundary square and commD, together with BoundaryProjection_fac, give comm. Each augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism as a resolution augmentation composed with an isomorphism; injectivity follows from the four InjectiveResolution.injective fields.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cartanEilenberg_rows (B : Type u) [Category.{v} B] [Abelian B] [EnoughInjectives B] (K : CochainComplex B ℤ) (hK : ∀ p : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (K.X p)) : let S := ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K ∃ R : CartanEilenbergRows S, (∀ p : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (R.A p)) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (R.jA p) ∧ QuasiIso (R.jZ p) ∧ QuasiIso (R.jD p) ∧ QuasiIso (R.jH p)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), Injective ((R.A p).X q) ∧ Injective ((R.Z p).X q) ∧ Injective ((R.D p).X q) ∧ Injective ((R.H p).X q))
